props.gloss_en: Reish Lakish: the Sages decreed impurity on glass vessels since their making begins from sand
the Sages made glass vessels like earthenware vessels (Reish Lakish; re-asserted by Rav Ashi at 16b.1: לעולם לכלי חרס דמו)
the mishna: these interpose in [the immersion of] vessels -- pitch and myrrh on glass vessels
the stam: the mishna speaks of glass vessels that were perforated and he dripped lead into them
the stam: and [that mishna] is R' Meir's
R' Meir: everything follows the facilitator (המעמיד)
R' Meir (as RSBG reports): glass vessels that were perforated and had lead dripped into them are impure
the Sages (as RSBG reports): they are pure

the mishna: earthenware and natron vessels are alike in impurity -- they become impure and render impure from their airspace, become impure from behind, do not become impure from their outer side, and their breaking purifies them
the stam (אמרי): since, when broken, they can be repaired, the Sages made glass vessels like metal vessels
the mishna: metal vessels, flat and receptacles, are [susceptible to becoming] impure; broken, they become pure; remade into vessels, they revert to their old impurity
the mishna: wooden, leather, bone and glass vessels -- broken, they become pure; remade into vessels, they are susceptible to impurity from now on
the same mishna: their flat vessels are pure [not susceptible], their receptacles impure
the stam: the impurity of glass vessels is rabbinic
the stam: and old impurity is rabbinic
the stam: on Torah-law impurity the Sages imposed [old] impurity; on rabbinic impurity they did not
the stam: for flat metal vessels are [susceptible] by Torah law
the stam: the Sages made a distinguishing mark in them, so that teruma and consecrated food not be burned on their account
Rav Ashi: [glass becomes impure from its outer side] since its inside is seen like its outside
Shimon ben Shatach instituted the ketuba for a woman
and he decreed impurity on metal vessels
the stam: metal vessels are [susceptible to impurity] by Torah law
as it is written: 'only the gold and the silver...' (Num 31:22)
the stam: [Shimon ben Shatach's decree] was needed only for old impurity

Rav: there was an incident with Shel Tziyyon the queen, who made a feast for her son; all her vessels became impure, and she broke them and gave them to the smith, who welded them and made new vessels of them
and the Sages said: they revert to their old impurity
the stam: why [old impurity]? because of the fence of the water of purification they touched it
an unnamed view: they said [old impurity] not of all impurities, but of corpse impurity alone
an unnamed view: they said [old impurity] of all impurities
Abaye: a decree lest he not perforate it [enough] to make it pure
Rava: a decree lest they say immersion that same day suffices for it
the stam: what is between them? -- the case where he smashed it completely

supports.gloss_en: דתניא: כלי זכוכית שנקבו והטיף לתוכן אבר, אמר רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: רבי מאיר מטמא וחכמים מטהרין -- R' Meir treats the lead-sealed glass as the lead determines
דכתיב: אך את הזהב ואת הכסף וגו׳ (Num 31:22)
דאמר רב יהודה אמר רב: מעשה בשל ציון המלכה ... ואמרו חכמים: יחזרו לטומאתן ישנה

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה לא תהא להן טהרה במקוה, אלמה תנן: ואלו חוצצין בכלים -- הזפת והמור בכלי זכוכית -- if glass were like earthenware it could not be purified in a mikveh, yet the mishna speaks of interpositions in immersing glass vessels

answered_by.gloss_en: הכא במאי עסקינן -- perforated glass vessels sealed with lead, and the mishna is R' Meir's, for whom all follows the facilitator (= p_okimta_nikvu_ever, p_mishna_kerabbi_meir, p_rm_hakol_achar_hamaamid)

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה לא ליטמו מגבן, אלמה תנן: כלי חרס וכלי נתר טומאתן שוה ... כלי נתר וכלי חרס הוא דטומאתן שוה, אבל מידי אחרינא -- לא! -- if glass were like earthenware it would not become impure from its outer side; the mishna equates only natron with earthenware, nothing else

answered_by.gloss_en: אמרי: כיון דכי נשתברו יש להם תקנה, שוינהו ככלי מתכות -- since broken glass can be repaired, the Sages made it like metal vessels (= p_zechuchit_kematachot)

רב אשי אמר: לעולם לכלי חרס דמו, ודקא קשיא לך לא ליטמו מגבן -- הואיל ונראה תוכו כברו -- glass is like earthenware after all; it is impure from its outer side because its inside is seen like its outside (= p_nireh_tocho_kebaro)

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה יחזרו לטומאתן ישנה ככלי מתכות? דתנן: כלי מתכות ... חזרו לטומאתן ישנה (= p_mishna_matachot_chozrin), ואילו גבי כלי זכוכית תנן: ... מקבלין טומאה מכאן ולהבא -- מכאן ולהבא אין, למפרע לא -- glass, unlike metal, does not revert to its old impurity

answered_by.gloss_en: טומאת כלי זכוכית דרבנן, וטומאה ישנה דרבנן -- the Sages imposed old impurity on Torah-law impurity, not on rabbinic impurity (= p_tumat_zechuchit_derabanan, p_tumah_yeshana_derabanan, p_tumah_yeshana_bedeoraita)

objections.gloss_en: פשוטיהן מיהא ליטמו, דהא פשוטי כלי מתכות דאורייתא נינהו? -- if glass is like metal, its flat vessels at least should be impure, since flat metal vessels are Torah-law [and 16a.3's rabbinic line would not exempt them]

answered_by.gloss_en: עבדי בהו רבנן היכירא, כי היכי דלא לישרוף עלייהו תרומה וקדשים (= p_heker_teruma_vekodashim)

objections.gloss_en: כלי מתכות דאורייתא נינהו! דכתיב: אך את הזהב ואת הכסף וגו׳ -- metal vessels are impure by Torah law (kind svara under protest: the objection cites a verse, which has no ObjectionKind)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא נצרכה אלא לטומאה ישנה -- the decree was needed only for old impurity (= p_sbs_tumah_yeshana), as in Rav's incident of Shel Tziyyon

objections.gloss_en: הניחא למאן דאמר לא לכל הטומאות אמרו אלא לטומאת המת בלבד -- שפיר; אלא למאן דאמר לכל הטומאות אמרו, מאי איכא למימר? -- the water-of-purification fence explains old impurity only for corpse impurity; for the all-impurities view another reason is needed

answered_by.gloss_en: גזירה שמא לא יקבנו בכדי טהרתו (= p_abaye_shema_lo_yikbenu)
גזירה שמא יאמרו טבילה בת יומא עולה לה (= p_rava_tevila_bat_yoma)
